evidence.statement: The authors report immunizing one llama with HEK293 membranes expressing mGlyR, collecting blood 87 days after immunization, and amplifying leukocyte-derived VHH cDNA.
The amplified cDNA was cloned into pCANTAB5 to produce a phage-displayed nanobody library in E. coli TG1.
The library was depleted on mock-transfected HEK293 membranes and selected on mGlyR-expressing membranes. The authors report three panning rounds and 61 individual clones for screening.
The cDNA-constructs Methods explicitly include Nb20 among promising candidates subcloned from the phage-display workflow into pET28a and provide its complete sequence.
The general nanobody production Methods describe C-terminal c-myc and 8xHis tags. This passage does not explicitly identify the deposited N-terminal prefix as the cryo-EM reagent.

interpretations.statement: These linked Methods establish the authors’ reported immune-library discovery route for Nb20. They do not supply a complete genealogical comparison against development or census binders and therefore do not establish the absence of shared ancestry.
The 61 screened clones are a source-level discovery inventory, not 61 benchmark cases or independent eligible groups.
